points.title: 早年教育
points.description: 威廉·汤姆森（后来的开尔文勋爵）出生于北爱尔兰贝尔法斯特的一个学术世家。父亲詹姆斯·汤姆森是数学教授，对儿子的早期教育有着深远影响。威廉从小就展现出非凡的数学天赋，10岁进入格拉斯哥大学预科，11岁开始正式学习大学课程。这段早期教育为他日后的科学成就奠定了坚实基础，特别是培养了他对数学和物理学的浓厚兴趣。
points.descriptionEn: William Thomson (later Lord Kelvin) was born in Belfast, Ireland, into an academic family. His father, James Thomson, was a mathematics professor who profoundly influenced his early education. Thomson showed exceptional mathematical talent from a young age, entering Glasgow University's preparatory department at age 10 and beginning formal university studies at 11. This early education laid the foundation for his future scientific achievements, particularly nurturing his deep interest in mathematics and physics.

points.title: 剑桥深造
points.description: 1841年，汤姆森进入剑桥大学彼得学院学习。在这里，他接触到了当时最前沿的数学和物理学理论，特别是法国数学家的热力学研究。1845年，他以优异成绩毕业并获得史密斯奖。剑桥的学习经历极大地拓展了他的学术视野，为他后来在热力学领域的开创性工作奠定了理论基础。同时，他在这里结识了许多重要的科学界人物，建立了广泛的学术联系。
points.descriptionEn: In 1841, Thomson entered Peterhouse, Cambridge University. There, he was exposed to the most advanced mathematical and physical theories of the time, particularly French thermodynamics research. He graduated with honors and won the Smith Prize in 1845. His Cambridge experience significantly broadened his academic horizons, laying the theoretical foundation for his later pioneering work in thermodynamics. He also met many important scientific figures and established extensive academic connections.

points.title: 教授生涯
points.description: 1846年，年仅22岁的汤姆森被任命为格拉斯哥大学自然哲学教授，这一职位他一直担任到1899年。在格拉斯哥大学，他建立了世界上第一个物理实验室，改革了物理教学方法。他提出了绝对温标（开尔文温标），奠定了热力学第二定律的基础，并提出了能量耗散理论。他还参与了跨大西洋电缆的铺设工程，解决了长距离电报信号衰减问题，因此被封为爵士。这一时期是他学术生涯的黄金时期，多项重要成果都在此期间完成。
points.descriptionEn: In 1846, at just 22 years old, Thomson was appointed Professor of Natural Philosophy at the University of Glasgow, a position he held until 1899. At Glasgow, he established the world's first physics laboratory and reformed physics teaching methods. He proposed the absolute temperature scale (Kelvin scale), laid the foundation for the second law of thermodynamics, and developed the theory of energy dissipation. He also participated in the laying of the transatlantic telegraph cable, solving the problem of signal attenuation over long distances, and was knighted for this work. This period represented the golden age of his academic career, with many important achievements completed during this time.

points.title: 贵族生涯
points.description: 1892年，汤姆森因其在科学和工程领域的杰出贡献，被维多利亚女王授予开尔文勋爵称号，成为英国贵族。此后他更多地参与国家科学政策的制定，担任英国皇家学会会长等重要职务。在伦敦期间，他继续科学研究，同时也更多地关注科学教育改革和国家科技发展政策。他的社会地位显著提高，成为维多利亚时代科学界的标志性人物之一，经常受邀参与国家重大科技决策。
points.descriptionEn: In 1892, Thomson was awarded the title of Baron Kelvin of Largs by Queen Victoria for his outstanding contributions to science and engineering. As a member of the British nobility, he became more involved in national science policy, serving as President of the Royal Society and other important positions. During his time in London, he continued his scientific research while also focusing on science education reform and national technology development policies. His social status significantly increased, making him one of the iconic figures of the Victorian scientific community, frequently consulted on major national technological decisions.

points.title: 晚年研究
points.description: 开尔文勋爵晚年主要在苏格兰拉格斯度过。尽管年事已高，他仍然活跃在科学前沿，对地球年龄、电子理论等新兴领域保持浓厚兴趣。他提出了地球年龄的估算方法，虽然后来被证明低估了地球的实际年龄，但在当时具有开创性意义。他还对X射线和电子等新发现进行了研究。这一时期，他更多地回顾自己的科学生涯，总结经验，同时关注年轻一代科学家的培养，为科学事业的发展继续贡献力量。
points.descriptionEn: In his later years, Lord Kelvin primarily lived in Largs, Scotland. Despite his advanced age, he remained active at the forefront of science, maintaining keen interest in emerging fields such as Earth's age and electron theory. He proposed methods for estimating Earth's age, which although later proven to underestimate the planet's actual age, were pioneering at the time. He also conducted research on new discoveries like X-rays and electrons. During this period, he reflected on his scientific career, summarized his experiences, and focused on nurturing younger scientists, continuing to contribute to the advancement of science.

supporter.zh: 开尔文勋爵是19世纪最伟大的物理学家之一，他的科学贡献跨越热力学、电磁学、地球物理学等多个领域。他提出的绝对温标至今仍是国际标准，热力学第二定律的建立改变了人们对能量转换的认识。作为跨大西洋电缆工程的技术指导，他解决了长距离通信的关键难题，推动了全球化进程。他还是一位杰出的教育家，建立了世界上第一个物理实验室，改革了物理教学方法，培养了众多优秀科学家。
supporter.en: Lord Kelvin stands as one of the greatest physicists of the 19th century, with scientific contributions spanning thermodynamics, electromagnetism, geophysics, and other fields. His absolute temperature scale remains an international standard today, and his establishment of the second law of thermodynamics revolutionized understanding of energy transformation. As technical advisor for the transatlantic cable project, he solved critical problems in long-distance communication, advancing globalization. He was also an exceptional educator, establishing the world's first physics laboratory and reforming teaching methods, nurturing numerous outstanding scientists.

critic.zh: 开尔文勋爵的晚年科学判断受到批评，他坚决反对原子理论，低估了地球的实际年龄，对X射线和电子等新发现持怀疑态度。他在科学上的保守立场使他错过了物理学革命的重要机遇。此外，他在跨大西洋电缆项目中获得的巨额专利费也引发了关于科学伦理的争议。作为贵族，他的社会地位有时影响了他的科学判断，使他难以完全摆脱维多利亚时代的社会偏见。
critic.en: Lord Kelvin's late scientific judgments faced criticism, as he staunchly opposed atomic theory, underestimated Earth's actual age, and remained skeptical of new discoveries like X-rays and electrons. His conservative scientific stance caused him to miss important opportunities during the physics revolution. Additionally, the substantial patent fees he received for the transatlantic cable project raised questions about scientific ethics. As a nobleman, his social status sometimes influenced his scientific judgments, making it difficult for him to completely摆脱 Victorian social prejudices.

objective.zh: 在历史学界，开尔文勋爵被视为连接经典物理学与现代物理学的桥梁人物。他的工作既代表了维多利亚时代科学成就的巅峰，也预示了20世纪物理学革命的到来。流行文化中，他常被描绘为典型的维多利亚时代绅士科学家形象，体现了当时科学与社会地位的紧密联系。他的名字已成为温度单位，成为科学界永恒的象征。尽管他的某些观点后来被证明是错误的，但他的科学方法和创新精神仍然影响着后世科学家。
objective.en: In historical scholarship, Lord Kelvin is viewed as a bridge figure connecting classical and modern physics. His work represents both the pinnacle of Victorian scientific achievement and foreshadowed the 20th-century physics revolution. In popular culture, he is often portrayed as the archetype of the Victorian gentleman scientist, reflecting the close connection between science and social status of that era. His name has become a temperature unit, an eternal symbol in the scientific community. Although some of his views were later proven incorrect, his scientific methods and innovative spirit continue to influence later generations of scientists.

self.zh: 当我无法衡量某物时，我对它的认识就非常贫乏；当我能够衡量它时，我就对它有了充分的认识。
self.en: When I can measure something and express it in numbers, I know something about it; but when I cannot measure it and express it in numbers, my knowledge is of a meager and unsatisfactory kind.

others.zh: 开尔文勋爵是19世纪物理学界的巨人，他的工作为现代物理学奠定了基础，尽管他未能预见即将到来的革命性变化。
others.en: Lord Kelvin was a giant of 19th-century physics whose work laid the foundation for modern physics, though he failed to foresee the revolutionary changes that were about to come.
